PLAINTIFF'S CASE:

Page no.3/18 proportionate rights in the land underneath vide three separate registered Sale Deeds dated 25.11.2003.
3.

The defendants no.1 and 3 are carrying on illegal business of supply of water jugs by refrigerating bore-well water from shop/godown no.1 and 2 at ground floor of the suit property in active connivance of all other defendants.
No permission has been obtained by the defendants no.1 and 3 from the defendants no.4, 5, 8 and 11 and other concerned authorities for the same.
The defendants no.1 and 3 have no right or authority to use underground water resources for commercial sale.
The defendants no.1 and 3 are using the electricity directly by committing theft of electricity of the defendant no.7 and have been misusing the same for commercial purposes.
Defendants no.1 and 3 have also not obtained any licence from defendants no.6, 8 and 11 for supplying refrigerated drinking water through jugs/bottles.

Defendants no.1 and 3 have illegally and unauthorizedly broken the side wall of the shop/godown no.2 and captured the common toilet & passage for storing the water jugs etc. and locked the main gate of the said portion for committing theft of electricity and water from the common toilet so that no one other then the defendants no.1 and 3 can use the common toilet and passage at ground floor of the suit property.
Therefore, the plaintiffs are facing great hardship due to aforesaid acts of the defendants no.1 and 3.

Previously also, the defendants no.1 and 3 had blocked the common passage and toilet against which the plaintiff no.1 had lodged several complaints with the local authorities and served the defendants no.1, 10 and 11 with the legal notice dated 08.06.2012.

The plaintiffs had lodged complaints with the defendants no.8 to 11 against the defendants no.1 and 3 on different dates but all in vain.

Therefore, the plaintiffs as well as their tenants are suffering a lot as their day to day business is being hampered and the acts of defendants no. 1 and 3 are also causing nuisance and health hazard to the plaintiffs and also monetary losses.

Hence, the plaintiffs filed the present suit for permanent and mandatory injunction against the defendants seeking the following reliefs :
I. A decree of mandatory injunction thereby directing the defendants no.1 and 3 to immediately restore the wall of the shop/godown no.2 of the suit property and to remove the water jugs/bottles which are being illegally and unauthorizedly stored by the defendants no.1 and 3 in the common toilet and passage at the ground floor of the suit property.

II. A decree of mandatory injunction thereby directing the defendants no. 4 to 11 to take necessary, proper and immediate action against the illegal and unauthorized acts of the defendants CS DJ No.11985/16 Vimal Kumar Goyal & Anr. Vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma & Ors.

III. A decree of permanent injunction thereby restraining the defendants no.1 and 3 from parking any cycle rickshaw in the gali in front of the suit property.

IV. A decree for a sum of Rs.3,29,000/- towards damages and losses suffered by the plaintiffs and their tenants till the date of filing of the suit and a sum of Rs.1000/- per day from the date of filing of the suit till restoration of the wall of the shop/godown no.2 of the suit property towards passage and removal of the nuisance and encroachment from the ground floor of the suit property.
DEFENDANT'S CASE:
5. Defendant no.1 and 3 filed their joint Written Statement preliminarily objecting to the suit of the plaintiffs on the ground that the plaintiffs are not the owners of the suit property and even denied the ownership rights of the plaintiffs in respect to the land underneath and common toilet, passage,
stair cases and walls.

It is stated that three Sale Deeds all dated 25.11.2003 in respect of the three godowns of the suit property were executed, however, sale consideration mentioned in the said Sale Deeds were never paid by the plaintiffs.
In fac, the cheques mentioned in the Sale Deeds were never presented for encashment at the request of the plaintiffs because the plaintiffs promised to issue fresh cheques.
However, later on the plaintiffs back tracked and did not pay sale consideration to the owners of these three godown i.e. CS DJ No.11985/16 Vimal Kumar Goyal & Anr. Vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma & Ors.

The right, title or interest in respect of the suit property is deemed to have not been created and/or conferred upon the plaintiffs.

Whether the plaintiff is entitled to a decree of mandatory injunction as prayed?
OPP 30.
The onus to prove this issue was on the plaintiffs.
The plaintiffs had sought three kinds of mandatory injunctions against defendants no.1 and 3 as well as defendants no.4 to 11.

However, as per the statement of the plaintiffs made on 15.11.2025 the only mandatory injunction that he is now seeking is a direction to defendants no.1 and 3 to immediately restore the wall of the shop/godown no.2 in the suit property as shown in site plan Ex.PW-5/5 at point XY.
The other reliefs of mandatory injunctions have already become infructuous.
31. It is the case of the plaintiffs that they had purchased three shops/ godowns in the suit property bearing no.5, 6 and 7 from the defendants no.1 and 3.
As per their Sale Deeds Ex.PW-1/1 to Ex.PW-1/3, they were entitled to use the common toilet and common passage on the ground floor of the suit property.
It is also an admitted case of the plaintiffs that shops no.1 and 2 are in the possession of defendants no. 1 and 3.
The grievance of the plaintiffs is that defendants no.1 and 3 had demolished a small portion of the wall shown at point XY making an entry into shop no.1 and 2 from the common passage and vice versa.

It is the case of the plaintiff that by removing the wall at Vimal Kumar Goyal vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma on 28 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29460548/
8 XY shown in site plan Ex.PW-5/5, defendants no.1 and 3 have been using the common passage for storing water jugs etc because of which the right of the plaintiffs to use the common passage is being effected.

sentences.text: 32. Perusal of the site plan shows that shop no. 4 to 7 on the ground floor of the suit property are on the left side.
There is a common toilet and staircase just adjacent to shop no. 4 on the right side while shop no. 5, 6 and 7 belonging to the plaintiffs are on the left side of shop no. 4.
Adjacent to the common toilet there is a common passage towards the right side of the toilet.
The opening of the toilet is from the common passage.
On the right side of the common passage are the shop no.1 and 2 belonging to defendants no.1 and 3.
The opening/entrance of all the shops are from the front gali as shown in the site plan Ex. PW-5/5.
As per the case of the plaintiff, the defendants no.1 and 3 had made a small opening by breaking the wall at point XY between the common passage and shop no.1 and 2.
The plaintiffs are seeking closing of the wall and restoring it to its original position.

However,
despite specific query from the plaintiffs, they have been unable to explain as to how this opening at point XY is effecting their easmentary rights in the common passage adjacent to the shop no.1 and 2.
This opening is not towards or in the wall of shop belonging to the plaintiffs.

Again the allegation that by making this opening, defendants no.1 and 3 are in any manner restraining the free use of the common passage by the plaintiffs by keeping water jugs and other articles is no longer continuing as per the own admissions of the plaintiffs.

It is also an admitted case of the plaintiffs that shop no.1 and 2 is belonging to defendants no.1 and 3 and accordingly unless any easmentary rights of the plaintiffs are being CS DJ No.11985/16 Vimal Kumar Goyal & Anr. Vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma &
Ors. Page no.15/18 effected, the defendants no.1 and 3 cannot be directed to close the opening at point XY as shown in site plan Ex. PW-5/5.

sentences.text: The plaintiffs have miserably failed to show any such disturbance in his easementry rights to use the common passage as shown in site plan Ex.PW5/5 due to the opening XY made by defendants no.1 and 3 in the left side wall of their shop no.182.
In these circumstances, I do not find any reason to direct defendants no.1 and 3 to close the opening shown at point XY in the site plan Ex. PW-5/5.
The mandatory injunction sought by the plaintiffs in this regard is accordingly denied.
33. In view of the findings given above, this issue is decided against the plaintiffs and in favour of the defendants.

ISSUE NO.3: Whether the plaintiff is entitled for recovery of a sum of Rs.3,20,000/- as damages?
OPP 34.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the plaintiffs.
